description: Deferred review items tracked across all phases. Each entry maps to a source review comment that was deemed reasonable but deferred to a later phase. Check this file at each phase integration gate to identify items that may have been resolved as a side effect of other work.

items.item: assertInside does not guard against symlink escape
items.detail: resolve() only handles literal '..' text traversal; a symlink inside the sandbox that points outside can be followed to escape the root, breaking R7 (file operations confined to the sandbox dir). Acceptable in Phase 0 as a local Mock, not a security boundary. Fix: validate the real path with realpathSync/fstat before allowing the operation.
items.notes: Resolved in task 1.4: shared path-guard.ts assertInside now canonicalizes root and target (nearest existing ancestor fallback for writes) with realpathSync, rejecting any symlink that redirects outside the root, plus dangling symlinks (target nonexistent) rejected via lstat during the walk-up — writes through a dangling escaping symlink are blocked. Used by both LocalTempSandbox and DockerSandbox. Covered by packages/runtime/sandbox/test/path-guard.test.ts (symlink read-escape, symlinked-parent write-escape, in-root symlink allowed, dangling final symlink, dangling symlinked parent). [2026-08-27 PR#17 review] TOCTOU between assertInside and the fs call remains (DEF-004), out of scope here.

items.item: teardown/write use hand-written dirnameOf/basenameOf string splitting
items.detail: Replace the hand-written dirnameOf/basenameOf string-splitting helpers with node:path dirname/basename for robustness and to avoid fragile edge cases.
items.notes: Resolved in task 1.4: local-temp-sandbox.ts teardown/write now use node:path dirname/basename; the hand-written helpers were removed.

items.item: Architecture doc §3 tools subdirectory naming (fs-server wording) inconsistent with implementation
items.detail: Implementation follows the AGENTS.md naming {fs,test,git,lint,sandbox} (user-decided); the architecture doc §3 originally used an fs-server wording. Migrated from the legacy embedded [DEF] in task 0.1 notes. Verified resolved during /pr-review-agora step 7: 系统架构设计文档.md no longer contains any fs-server wording (§3 is now a generic tools/ note).
items.notes: Legacy entry migrated per standing decision DEF (task notes keep only a ledger pointer).

items.item: TOCTOU symlink race (CWE-367) between path validation and fs operation
items.detail: WorktreeFsService performs a synchronous lexical path validation then a separate fs call; a concurrent process replacing the target/an ancestor with an escaping symlink between assertInside and readFileSync/writeFileSync can break R7 confinement. Definitive fix needs openat-under-trusted-fd or an isolated concurrently-writable worktree; Node 20 lacks a clean dir-relative open API and the change is too large for the PR scope.
items.notes: packages/tools/fs/src/fs-service.ts + worktree-registry.ts, plus the sandbox read/write path (LocalTempSandbox/DockerSandbox host-side read/write validate via assertInside then perform the fs call). Release condition: DockerSandbox (1.4) provides worktree isolation as mitigation; re-evaluate whether an openat refactor is needed when true parallelism lands (Phase 4 / 9.2). [2026-08-27] Mitigation landed in task 1.4: DockerSandbox confines run() to a per-task container (NetworkMode none, bind-mounted worktree root), so the concurrently-writable host dir is no longer the command execution boundary; sandbox read/write TOCTOU remains open for LocalTempSandbox-hosted fs operations, tracked here until Phase 4 re-evaluation. [2026-08-27 PR#17 review] CodeRabbit raised the same TOCTOU on the sandbox read/write path (local-temp-sandbox.ts:44); acknowledged, covered by this entry (definitive fix needs descriptor-relative no-follow ops or an isolated worktree — out of PR scope, deferred to Phase 4).

items.item: lint MCP server not implemented in Phase 1
items.detail: Phase 1 tool servers cover fs (1.1), test (1.2), git (1.3); packages/tools/lint is an empty stub and no lint server task exists in Phase 1. The §2 permission matrix declares lint for CODER/REVIEWER; the tool loader (task 1.5) must keep the RoleSpec.tools 'lint' entry resolvable-but-unavailable (skipped at registration), and Phase 1 exit tests must not require lint.
items.notes: User-approved deferral during task 1.5 planning ([2026-08-27]). RoleSpec.tools 'lint' stays declared in the whitelist matrix; the tool catalog has no lint entry so the loader registers nothing for it and logs the gap. When a lint MCP server lands (biome wrapper, Phase 2+), add a 'lint' catalog entry and the loader picks it up automatically.

items.item: TESTER git capability granularity: main-repo mutations vs worktree-scoped reads
items.detail: CodeRabbit flagged that TESTER (RoleSpec.tools includes 'git') is granted the full git group via LOGICAL_GROUPS — git_createWorktree + git_applyPatch + git_diff + git_merge — including main-repo mutations (createWorktree, merge) that go beyond the §2 matrix's 'git(worktree)' qualifier (worktree-scoped ops). The implementation is faithful to the matrix (TESTER git(worktree)=✓, full grant), so this is a spec-granularity decision, not a code bug: the bridge's single 'git' logical group cannot express read-only variants (ARCH=只读, REVIEWER=只读 diff are unrepresentable). Also resolved in PR #18 for Phase 0 by the PHASE0_TOOL_SURFACE gate (spec §9 '工具只接 fs + sandbox.run' — git phase-gated out of the Phase 0 runtime), so the over-grant only matters once git is exercised in Phase 1+. Resolution: split LOGICAL_GROUPS into worktree-scoped (git.applyPatch/git.diff) vs main-repo (git.createWorktree/git.merge) groups, or add 'git.readonly'→git.diff, per a human spec ruling on TESTER/ARCH/REVIEWER grants when the Phase 1 composition root lands.
items.notes: Deferred in /pr-review-agora for PR #18: requires a human spec decision on the §2 matrix granularity (does TESTER's git(worktree)=✓ include main-repo merge/createWorktree?). Phase 0 is already covered by the PHASE0_TOOL_SURFACE gate. When the Phase 1 composition root activates git tools, re-evaluate splitting the git group (read-only vs mutating) per this entry.

items.item: Review-pass convergence lacks leader confirmation in Phase 2 (humanGate lands in Phase 8)
items.detail: 详细设计 §3 convergence rule reads 'test 全过 + review 通过(经 leader 确认)', but humanGate (leader arbitration surface) is a Phase 8 deliverable. User ruled during task 2.2 planning ([2026-08-28]): Phase 2 simplifies convergence to 'REVIEWER pass → finalize' with no leader confirmation step; R3 (leader sole authority) is not violated because no agent auto-consensus replaces a leader ruling — the confirmation semantics simply do not exist yet.
items.notes: Resolution condition: when humanGate lands in Phase 8, wire REVIEWER-pass convergence through a leader confirmation gate (blocking humanGate per D4 terminate-and-fork) instead of finalizing directly. Check this entry at the Phase 8 exit gate.

items.item: Bind routing roster and WorkerRuntime roster into one source (composition-root ergonomics)
items.detail: CodeRabbit flagged that OrchestrationDeps.roster (routing) is independent from WorkerRuntimeDeps.roster (execution): a caller mismatching them makes decide() route PM/ARCHITECT/REVIEWER to a runtime whose specOf() throws UnknownRoleError. Verified in /pr-review-agora: the failure mode is a loud explicit UnknownRoleError (fail-fast, not silent corruption), and all current call sites (orchestrator.test orchestrationWith, lru-cache e2e, phase0-exit, phase1-exit ×2) pass PHASE0_ROSTER to both consistently. The task-2.2 user-approved plan explicitly chose 'OrchestrationDeps += roster? forwarded to decide()', so re-binding via a WorkerRuntime roster getter changes an approved interface design and needs a human ruling.
items.notes: Resolution condition: when the full 6-role composition root lands (DEFAULT_ROSTER first used outside unit tests), either expose the roster on WorkerRuntime and derive routing from it (drop OrchestrationDeps.roster), or validate roster coverage at the composition root. Requires human sign-off since it revises the task-2.2 approved DecideOptions/OrchestrationDeps design. Check this entry when Phase 3 composition work starts.

items.item: Idempotent re-escalation guard for resumed capped states (no duplicate escalation messages)
items.detail: CodeRabbit's merge-risk note: re-running a capped state (e.g. after a leader ruling that clears humanGate but not iterationCount) appends a second escalation message, because escalationMessage() mints a fresh msgId and deduplicatedAppend only dedups identical msgIds. Verified in /pr-review-agora: within a single runOrchestration the human_gate route halts immediately (exactly one escalation per run), and no current call site re-runs a capped state, so nothing duplicates today. The real exposure arrives in Phase 8, where humanGate switches to D4 terminate-and-fork and resumed states become routine.
items.notes: Resolution condition: when the Phase 8 humanGate body (terminate-and-fork per D4) lands, ensure state re-entry is idempotent end-to-end — either guard ifIterationLimit on 'humanGate already set with the same reason' or rebuild the escalation from the safePoint event cursor instead of re-appending. Check this entry when task 8.x humanGate implementation starts.

items.item: AppState.pendingPatch has no write op in the §1 Mutation union
items.detail: §1 defines pendingPatch (code-layer reference field) but the Mutation union lists no op for it — same gap class as #22/#25. Task 2.4 projection reads it read-only with an explicit null default (R9, no silent absence). Unlocked writers are consumer-driven per repo precedent (2.2 requirements, 2.4 conventions), and there is no real consumer yet: TESTER/REVIEWER consume worktree path refs via branchOrPatch.worktrees and can pull diffs themselves with git/fs tools (iron rule 2 — truth lives in the worktree).
items.notes: Resolution condition: unlock the pendingPatch set op when a real consumer lands — evaluate at task 2.5 e2e (does the CODER patch-submission flow need to carry patch metadata through State for the REVIEWER pendingDiff slice?), else slide to Phase 3 patch-reference work. Unlock follows the pre-paved path (SET_FIELDS + ENABLED_SET_FIELDS + applySet case with the non-array-object guard, signature unchanged) plus an R12 实装记录 in 详细设计方案 §1. The conventions half of Issue #25 was fixed in task 2.4 (PR #26). Check this entry at the Phase 2 exit gate (task 2.5).
